why: Several items mix fighting active attacks with repeated cleaning and repair, making the leading practice difficult to distinguish.

why.T3-072: The Sweden–Maryland partnership and reciprocal protection organize the retrospective, rather than a simple celebration of the flag. This is an item-is-a-bag: personal labour reports (T3-003), closing farewells (T3-117), discovery of the sub, and the song adaptation exceed one coherent additional placement.

why.T3-095: Most concepts identify or explain the moderators' switch through the date, reciprocal links and confused posting; these are tests of a moderators' change, not replies to member-staged fakes.
why.T3-023: Distinct concepts explain how to play the subject swap and defend enforcing it, beyond merely recognizing what happened.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Identifying the switch does not carry the instructions for performing crossover posts or the defence of enforced subject changes.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1345831 specifies how members should play inside the takeover, and C0038224 defends committing to its rules.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-023; dropping it would lose participation in and enforcement of the takeover.

why.T3-126: The initial problem is that repeaters do not yet form a group capable of answering outsiders or controlling the grid; this is not an organized room disowning rogues.
why.T3-005: Two distinct concepts rally the room against White Void erasure and insist the grid can still be saved.
why.T3-194: A member explicitly offers to negotiate with the other group and seeks its contact venue; no resulting agreement is shown.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: The absence of a group able to represent repeaters does not carry the later rally against an active erasure.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0762498 names the attack and calls members to band together; C1288371 urges saving the grid.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-005; dropping it would lose the active defensive rally.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Neither the lack of collective representation nor the defence call carries an individual's separate undertaking to negotiate with another group.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0321308 explicitly offers to negotiate once given the group's link.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-194; dropping it would lose the offered diplomatic errand.

why.T3-033: The item offers candidate marks, including a character, the Association logo and an ID card, without reporting a sustained build. It is an item-is-a-bag: choosing space (T3-020), debating capacity (T3-136), questioning absence and dismissing participation are distinct practices. T3-020 and T3-136 meet the additional three-concept floor.

why.T3-179: Members reject branding and flag ownership through anarchist opposition to intellectual property; the argument concerns ideology applied to the canvas, rather than the meaning of a particular symbol.

why.T3-038: The surviving title reports that work has started and locates that work in progress. It does not establish permission, conversion of the penguin, or a debate over possible locations.

why.T3-021: Repeated cleaning, monitoring and restoring the logo lead, including repair with attackers visible. This is an item-is-a-bag: distinct personal labour reports (T3-003), active fighting (T3-005), upkeep over expansion (T3-042), and sleep-related coverage (T3-141) each have their own concepts.

why.T3-065: The homeland flag's construction, dimensions, outline and repair lead and take precedence over generic building or design codes. This is an item-is-a-bag: emblem detailing (T3-113), correcting the separate Azores heart design (T3-004), repair of lettering and other details (T3-021), template enforcement and recognition of friendly mistakes are separately evidenced.

why.T3-009: Pride and the moment when the banner finally looks right mark the work as achieved, beyond encouragement to builders.
why.T3-164: Feeling publicly represented and crediting the banner with awareness express visibility through the work; the awareness claim remains the participant's interpretation.
why.T3-057: The cross-stitch is a new-medium remake, rather than a screenshot or other unchanged record.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Celebrating a successful banner does not carry the distinct experience of public representation or the participant's claim about awareness.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0567380 explicitly says the community is represented and present; C0850148 attributes visibility to the banner.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-164; dropping it would lose the expressed significance of ace visibility.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Neither celebration nor felt visibility records the separate act of reproducing the canvas flag in cross-stitch.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1273728 reports an actual cross-stitch inspired by the r/place Ace Pride Flag.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-057; dropping it would lose the material remake.

why.T3-017: Most concepts organize ordinary in-game Holo Pilot play and challenges for the date; nobody stages a false announcement in the room or changes the sub.
why.T3-048: Separate concepts anticipate developer-made April Fools features, wish for joke effects and remember an earlier official gag.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Planning community gameplay does not carry the separate anticipation and recollection of the developer's April Fools content.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1457321 asks about a special April Fools offering, C0772158 wishes for an official joke effect, and C0783576 recalls the earlier Prime titan gag.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-048; dropping it would lose the official-joke expectations and recollection.

why.T3-150: The offer is an ongoing alliance to maintain neighboring college logos, potentially bringing in Miami, rather than a one-off barter or a border settlement. Redirecting the proposal to FloridaGators establishes where that alliance must be considered.

why.T3-063: Moderators apply existing meme, repost, direct-link and relevance rules to canvas submissions. No gathering thread or change to those rules is proposed.

why.T3-030: The participant judges Rainbow Road's prior approval followed by destruction and consequently favors its opponents. This evaluates the worth of dealing with that group rather than invoking the approval to repair a current breach.

why.T3-033: Candidate first marks occupy the largest distinct concept set, including the football, scores, figures and team images; the later build does not override that count. This is an item-is-a-bag. Additional sets reaching three concepts are event explanation (T3-016), design work (T3-004), recruitment (T3-002), signing (T3-169), build progress (T3-038), upkeep (T3-021), defence (T3-005), overnight coverage (T3-141), scripts (T3-028), and achievement (T3-009). Smaller sets include chat setup, gathering the thread, further pieces and covering hate symbols.

why.T3-005: Calls to defend the border and reports of fighting an active attack give this item its main action, beyond routine flag repair. This is an item-is-a-bag: tracing attackers (T3-087) reaches three concepts, while homeland-flag upkeep, a proposed counter-script, time-zone coverage and survival celebration add distinct smaller practices.
